newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toyota says to resume near-normal output Friday.
newsitem.headline: Toyota says to resume near-normal output Friday.

text.p: Giant Japanese carmaker Toyota Motor Corp. expects to resume near-normal output levels at all its domestic production lines on Friday after a stoppage due to a fire at a parts maker over the weekend, a Toyota spokesman said Tuesday.
The fire on Saturday at a brake parts maker caused the idling of all Toyota's domestic plants Tuesday except for Daihatsu Motor Co. Ltd.
"We are sure to resume near-normal levels of vehicle production on Friday," a spokesman said.
Toyota has no plans to revise its finely coordinated "just in time" system for getting components delivered without holding excess inventories, he added.

Toyota produces cars and trucks at 30 domestic production lines including its affiliates, such as Daihatsu, with a total daily output rate of 14,000 vehicles. Toyota owns a 33.4 percent stake in Daihatsu.
Toyota had planned to raise its production rate to 16,000 vehicles per day in February and March due to expected strong demand ahead of Japan's consumption tax increase on April 1.
"We can raise the daily output to near the planned 16,000 units next Monday," the spokesman said.
Toyota has not disclosed how many vehicles it was unable to produce on Monday and Tuesday.
A decline in production in the four days to Thursday will be offset in the future by overtime or extra operations on holidays, the spokesman said.
